parsed.attack: The capture half of this loop is pure unrewarded cost and the payoff sits on the far side of a nine-month gap. A restorer photographs and narrates every bolt in weeks one to three while the novelty of the glasses is fresh, gets nothing back, and quietly stops around the point the frame is bare - and then reassembly, the only moment the product pays out, arrives to find a log that covers the first 30% of the teardown and is useless for the rest. Worse, the product's whole life is one project: when the bike runs, the job stops existing permanently unless the owner buys another wreck, so there is no second season for a $30 purchase to earn back in.
parsed.strongest_defence: Unlike most one-shot tools this one has a genuine built-in return trip - capture and consume are two halves of the same job, and the bag-of-bolts problem at reassembly is acute enough that the restorer comes back on his own, with a switching cost (the only record of what he did to this machine) that no competitor can reconstruct. A one-time purchase is priced honestly against a one-project lifetime, and the shareable teardown log posted to a forum is the acquisition loop, so the business never needed month-two usage from the same person.
parsed.verdict_reason: There is a real return moment at reassembly, but it is months of unrewarded logging away, which is exactly where capture habits die and where the record becomes too thin to return to.
